stemMarkdown: The price of an article is first increased by 45%, and then the new price is decreased by 38%. What is the net percentage change in price? (Enter a negative value if it is a net decrease.)
solutionMarkdown: Take the original price as 100. After a 45% increase: $100 \times (1 + 45/100) = 145.00$. After a 38% decrease on 145.00: $145.00 \times (1 - 38/100) = 89.90$. Net change $= 89.90 - 100 = -10.10\%$.
altSolutionMarkdown: Shortcut formula: net \% change $= p_1 - p_2 - \dfrac{p_1 p_2}{100} = 45 - 38 - \dfrac{1710}{100} = -10.10\%$.
